document.abstract: The International Telecommunications Union Radiocommunication Sector has recommended a broadcasting standard Recommendation ITU-R BT.2020 (Rec. 2020) for ultrahigh-definition television that is aimed at providing a better visual experience. It recommends a color gamut that exceeds previous broadcasting standards and is only achievable by laser-based display technologies. Quantum dot (QD)-enabled liquid crystal displays (LCDs) provide one alternative with potential to meet Rec. 2020's standard color gamut while taking advantage of existing manufacturing capacity. We examined how existing QD and LCD technology could be optimized to meet the Rec. 2020 color standard. Our analysis revealed that up to 94% gamut coverage can be achieved.

authors.bio: James (Jimmy) Thielen is a product development specialist, working in the Display and Material Systems Division at 3M Company since 2005. Thielen holds bachelor's degrees in electrical engineering and physics from the University of St. Thomas and a master's degree in management of technology from the University of Minnesota. Thielen has ten years of experience in the LED and display industries at 3M and has authored six published patents. He has also published in the American Journal of Physics, the Society of Information Displays Symposium, Photonics West Proceedings, the Journal of Vision and presented at the SMPTE Annual Technical Conference.
authors.name: James Thielen

authors.bio: James Hillis is a vision scientist in the Display Materials and Systems Division at 3M. He completed a Ph.D. in vision science at University of California, Berkeley, studying 3D shape perception before working on questions related to color perception as a post-doctoral fellow at the University of Pennsylvania. Prior to joining 3M, he worked as a faculty member at the University of Glasgow, where his research focused on social judgment and decision-making.
authors.name: James Hillis

authors.bio: John Van Derlofske received a Ph.D. in physics from the University of Alabama in Huntsville, where his thesis work concentrated on illumination systems design. After graduation, he worked as head optical designer for Chrysler, developing automotive lighting and illumination systems. Van Derlofske spent the next eight years at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, heading the Transportation Lighting Group at the Lighting Research Center. His responsibilities included research, curriculum development, and teaching graduate-level courses in lighting technology and design. Over the course of his academic and professional careers, Van Derlofske has authored 90 publications and given more than 50 presentations at national and international venues. Currently, Van Derlofske is a senior research specialist in 3M's Optical Systems Division Laboratory, where he works on the design, manufacturing, and application of light control films that make LCD displays brighter, more colorful and more efficient.
authors.name: John Van Derlofske

authors.bio: Dave Lamb is a senior physics research specialist working in the Optical Systems Division Laboratory at 3M Company since 2000. Lamb joined 3M upon completion of a doctorate in physics and post-doctoral research at the University of Alabama in Huntsville and NASA Marshall Space Flight Center. Lamb's current research focuses on display efficiency and the development of meaningful metrics for display of visual quality.
authors.name: Dave Lamb

authors.bio: Art Lathrop serves as a marketing development manager within the Display Materials and Systems Division of 3M, where he is responsible for the business development of 3M Quantum Dot Enhancement Film. Lathrop joined 3M in 2005. He also spent a year in 3M Korea's offices as the handheld application business development manager and multiple years supporting commercialization of multifunction films, 3D films, OLED light extraction, and multilayer reflectors. Lathrop received a bachelor's degree in psychology and East Asian studies from the College of William and Mary and a separate bachelor's degree in music performance (voice-opera) from Indiana University. He holds a master's degree in marketing and decision-support modeling from Kelley School of Business.
authors.name: Art Lathrop
